speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with generalized fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any changes in your urine color or the color of your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information; your history of ulcerative colitis, recent sexual activity with multiple partners, and inconsistent condom use are clinically relevant. Given your age and risk factors, could you tell me when your fatigue and itching first started relative to the diagnosis of your ulcerative colitis?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: 
Liver Function Panel: Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 7500/mm3, Platelet_Count 280,000/mm3, Na 138 mEq/L, K 4.7 mEq/L, Bilirubin_Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L, Anti-Nuclear_Antibody Negative, Antimitochondrial_Antibodies Negative.
Imaging: Abdominal_Ultrasound findings show thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The results show significant cholestatic liver injury with marked alkaline phosphatase elevation (460 U/L) and ductal thickening on ultrasound, suggesting an obstructive or infiltrative process. Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the specific imaging findings, have you experienced any episodes of abdominal pain in the upper right quadrant or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC).

The combination of cholestatic liver enzymes, bile duct wall thickening on ultrasound, severe pruritus, and your history of ulcerative colitis is pathognomonic for PSC. The negative ANA and AMA further exclude other autoimmune hepatopathies like primary biliary cholangitis or lupus.
